text:
mike: Heads up — p95 laddering in hosted-us-west started at ~09:12 UTC, lasted ~15m. p95 stepped from ~120ms -> ~480ms in ~5m intervals, p99 also climbed. queue depth on gpu-workers rose from 2 -> 20. not seeing rate limiter trigger. Anyone on infra?

aisha: :eyes: I'll pull queue and kernel metrics. can you paste a sample request id or a quick metric snapshot? any canary/rollout?

mike: No rollout. sample req id 01E3A9C2. quick metric: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/redwood/hosted | jq '.queues.us-west2[0].depth'` => 18 at peak.

sam: I'm seeing a KV cache eviction surge at the same wallclock. lots of small-prefix misses in the logs -> prefetch thrash suspicion. spinning up the profiler now.

sam: profiler snippet I grabbed:
```
kernel_selector: chosen=trt_int8 fallback=generic
batching_window_ms: 8 -> 32
avg_batch_size: 3 -> 10
kv_cache_misses_per_s: 240 -> 950
cpu_sys_pct: 12% -> 28%
```

eva: If the batching window jumped from 8 to 32ms the scheduler will accumulate larger batches -> higher queue_depth and bumped p95. need to know why batching window grew.

mario: There was a node replacement event at 09:10 (OOM on a noisy tenant job). kube-agent restarted a few inference containers; logs show `kernel_miss: fallback_to_generic` for 4 shards for ~90s.

aisha: fallback_to_generic would degrade single-token latencies and warm up the KV cache again. that can cascade into larger batches while trying to maintain throughput.

mike: I can reproduce locally: replay small 20-50 token requests at ~200 rps and watch p95 ladder while a shard toggles kernel to generic. i'll run a canary with kernel-affinity pinned.

devops-bot: rollback of the node pool completed at 09:28 UTC (auto-safety). event_id: rp-2026-09.

sam: hypothesis: node replace -> kernel selector fallback -> increased per-token time -> scheduler auto-increases batching_window to keep throughput -> queue_depth climbs -> tail latency laddering. rate limits not involved.

chrissy: Proposed action items:
- add a transient guard: do not expand `batching_window_ms` if `kernel_fallback_count` > 0 for a shard
- alert rule: `kv_cache_misses_per_s > 500 && queue_depth > 10` (P1)
- instrument traces to include `kernel_fallback` markers and `batching_window_ms` at request start
- short-term: pin kernel-affinity for the affected fleet while we harden selector
I'll file an infra ticket.

mike: assigning to @chrissy and @sam. i'll attach the full profiler dumps and request traces in the ticket.

chrissy: filing INC-7842 with logs + profiler + repro steps now. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks all — will monitor for recurrence and report back once canary finishes.
